views.name: analytics.hiv_observation_fact_v1
views.grain: Demo-only HIV care observation fact at exactly one row per FHIR Observation, pivoting each coding system (CIEL / SNOMED / WHO-ANC) into its own column from the lossless observation_flat base. concept_name comes from the OpenMRS-native coding's display. A row carries a numeric, coded, text, boolean, or datetime value depending on the concept. Only observations whose subject resolves to an ingested Patient appear (subject-less rows are excluded by the patient join). Dataset notes: HIV viral load has only 3 recorded results in this instance (CD4 count and CD4% are the well-populated quantitative markers), and HIV status is not recorded as a Condition — questions about patients with HIV or on treatment must use the Antiretroviral plan/use or Current WHO HIV stage concepts.

columns.description: FHIR Observation resource identifier and stable row identity.

columns.name: patient_id
columns.description: FHIR Patient resource identifier referenced by the observation.

columns.name: encounter_id
columns.description: FHIR Encounter resource identifier the observation was recorded within.

columns.name: patient_gender
columns.description: FHIR Patient.gender.

columns.name: patient_birth_date
columns.description: FHIR Patient.birthDate. Compute age at observation as (observed_at - patient_birth_date) rather than assuming a stored age column.

columns.name: obs_status
columns.description: FHIR Observation.status.

columns.name: observed_at
columns.description: FHIR Observation effective dateTime.

columns.name: concept_name
columns.description: Human-readable concept display name from the OpenMRS-native coding; populated on every row regardless of which terminology mappings exist. This is the reliable way to select a concept: a question naming a marker must constrain this field.

columns.name: concept_code_ciel
columns.description: CIEL numeric code for the observed concept (e.g. 5497 for CD4 count). Coverage verified against the complete dataset: 99.9% of observations carry a CIEL coding; a small residue does not, so concept_name (which is populated on every row and carries the semantic aliases) remains the primary way to select a concept, with this column for terminology filtering and cross-reference.

columns.name: concept_code_snomed
columns.description: SNOMED CT code for the observed concept when the source carries a SNOMED coding. Cross-reference/terminology column; coverage is partial, as with CIEL.

columns.name: concept_code_who_anc
columns.description: WHO ANC custom code (http://fhir.org/guides/who/anc-cds) for the observed concept when present. Cross-reference/terminology column; sparse.

columns.name: value_numeric
columns.description: Populated only for numeric-valued concepts (e.g. CD4 count, CD4%, CD8 count). Null for coded, text, boolean, or datetime observations; do not aggregate across unlike concepts or units.

columns.name: value_unit
columns.description: Unit for value_numeric, when the source Observation carries one.

columns.name: value_coded_name
columns.description: Human-readable label for a coded answer (e.g. Yes/No/Unknown for antiretroviral use, a WHO stage, an adherence category), from the OpenMRS-native coding; populated for every coded-valued observation.

columns.name: value_coded_code_ciel
columns.description: CIEL numeric code for the coded answer when the source carries one; near-complete coverage, same residue caveat as concept_code_ciel. value_coded_name is populated on every coded row.

columns.name: value_coded_code_snomed
columns.description: SNOMED CT code for the coded answer when the source carries one; cross-reference column.

columns.name: value_text
columns.description: Free-text value, for the small number of concepts recorded as plain text.

columns.name: value_boolean
columns.description: Boolean value, for yes/no concepts recorded as FHIR valueBoolean (e.g. screening flags).

columns.name: value_datetime
columns.description: Datetime value, for concepts recorded as FHIR valueDateTime (e.g. return-visit or event dates).

views.name: analytics.hiv_medication_request_fact_v1
views.grain: Demo-only HIV medication request fact at exactly one row per FHIR MedicationRequest (collapsing the medication/statusReason coding cross product on the base table, and de-duplicating medication_flat before the join so a drug with several codings cannot multiply the request). Requests whose subject does not resolve to an ingested Patient are excluded by the patient join. MedicationRequest carries no date in this export, so there is no time window here; join hiv_visit_fact_v1 on encounter_id when a date is needed. medication_code_openmrs/ciel/snomed/who_anc pivot each terminology system into its own column, like hiv_concept_mapping_v1, so a multi-coded medication cannot pair a code with the wrong system; medication_name may be null when no arm supplies one -- see catalog-overlay.json.

columns.name: medication_request_id
columns.description: FHIR MedicationRequest resource identifier and stable row identity.

columns.name: patient_id
columns.description: FHIR Patient resource identifier the medication was requested for.

columns.name: patient_gender
columns.description: FHIR Patient.gender of the requested-for patient.

columns.name: patient_birth_date
columns.description: FHIR Patient.birthDate. MedicationRequest carries no date here, so age at request cannot be derived from this view alone.

columns.name: encounter_id
columns.description: FHIR Encounter the request was recorded within. Join hiv_visit_fact_v1 on this to get a date.

columns.name: request_status
columns.description: FHIR MedicationRequest.status, for example active, completed or stopped.

columns.name: request_intent
columns.description: FHIR MedicationRequest.intent, for example order or plan.

columns.name: do_not_perform
columns.description: True when the request records that the medication should NOT be taken. Exclude these when counting prescriptions.

columns.name: medication_name
columns.description: Drug name, by precedence: the request's own reference display, its direct coding display, the referenced Medication's text, then the referenced Medication's coding display. Null when none of those is populated -- verified nonempty in the current data, but not guaranteed by the source.

columns.name: medication_code_openmrs
columns.description: OpenMRS-native drug code (no external coding system), from the request's own coding when present, otherwise the referenced Medication's.

columns.name: medication_code_ciel
columns.description: CIEL numeric drug code, from the request's own coding when present, otherwise the referenced Medication's. Null when neither carries a CIEL mapping.

columns.name: medication_code_snomed
columns.description: SNOMED CT drug code, from the request's own coding when present, otherwise the referenced Medication's. Null when neither carries a SNOMED mapping.

columns.name: medication_code_who_anc
columns.description: WHO ANC custom drug code, from the request's own coding when present, otherwise the referenced Medication's. Null when neither carries a WHO ANC mapping; sparse in this data (at most one drug carries it).

views.name: analytics.hiv_visit_fact_v1
views.grain: Demo-only HIV care visit fact at exactly one row per FHIR Encounter (collapsing the type/participant/location coding cross product; encounters without a resolvable Patient subject are excluded by the patient join). days_since_prior_visit is computed across this view's own 2020-2035 window, so a query that further narrows started_at still sees the real gap; it is null only for a patient's first encounter inside the window.

columns.name: encounter_id
columns.description: FHIR Encounter resource identifier and stable row identity.

columns.name: patient_id
columns.description: FHIR Patient resource identifier referenced by the encounter.

columns.name: patient_gender
columns.description: FHIR Patient.gender.

columns.name: patient_birth_date
columns.description: FHIR Patient.birthDate.

columns.name: encounter_status
columns.description: FHIR Encounter.status.

columns.name: encounter_type
columns.description: FHIR Encounter type display name; almost all encounters in this demo instance are OPD Visit.

columns.name: started_at
columns.description: FHIR Encounter.period.start.

columns.name: ended_at
columns.description: FHIR Encounter.period.end.

columns.name: prior_visit_started_at
columns.description: started_at of this patient's immediately preceding visit in this view; null for a patient's first visit in the 2020-2035 window.

columns.name: days_since_prior_visit
columns.description: Days between this visit and the patient's immediately preceding visit. Real, patient-specific spacing (some patients visit monthly with gaps, some have single-day visit pairs); it is not a fixed or uniform interval. Null for a patient's first visit.

columns.name: snomed_code
columns.description: SNOMED CT code mapped to this concept, when present.

columns.description: WHO ANC custom code mapped to this concept, when present.

columns.name: observation_count
columns.description: Number of observations carrying exactly this mapping combination.

views.name: analytics.hiv_patient_dim_v1
views.grain: Demo-only patient dimension at exactly one row per FHIR Patient. Join to any fact view on patient_id. Prefer this over public.patient_flat, which repeats a patient once per name, identifier, and practitioner.

columns.name: patient_id
columns.description: FHIR Patient resource identifier and stable row identity; the join key every fact view references.

columns.name: gender
columns.description: FHIR Patient.gender, constant per resource.

columns.name: birth_date
columns.description: FHIR Patient.birthDate. Compute age as (reference date - birth_date) rather than assuming a stored age column.

columns.name: family_name
columns.description: FHIR Patient.name.family -- the surname, and what a request for a patient last name means. Populated only when the patient has exactly one distinct nonblank family name; null when the source carries several, because choosing one would invent a person. Demo data: treat as identifying information.

columns.name: given_name
columns.description: FHIR Patient.name.given -- the first name. Populated only when the patient has exactly one distinct nonblank given name, on the same rule as family_name, and resolved independently of it. Demo data: treat as identifying information.

views.name: public.patient_flat
views.grain: Raw FHIR Patient, one row per patient x name x given x identifier x general practitioner. A patient repeats: never count rows here as patients. Prefer analytics.hiv_patient_dim_v1, which is exactly one row per patient and carries family_name and given_name; use this table only when you need an identifier, an organization, or a practitioner the dimension does not expose. Contains identifying information.

columns.name: id
columns.description: FHIR Patient resource identifier. Repeats across rows; joins to patient_id on every other relation.

columns.name: active
columns.description: FHIR Patient.active. Null when the source did not state it, which is not the same as inactive.

columns.name: gender
columns.description: FHIR Patient.gender, constant per patient.

columns.name: birth_date
columns.description: FHIR Patient.birthDate, constant per patient. Compute age as (reference date - birth_date).

columns.name: practitioner_id

columns.name: family
columns.description: FHIR Patient.name.family -- the surname. Repeats per name record, and a patient with two name records has two values here, so selecting one at random invents a person. Prefer analytics.hiv_patient_dim_v1.family_name, which is null unless the patient has exactly one. Identifying information.

columns.name: given
columns.description: FHIR Patient.name.given -- the first name, with the same repetition risk as family. Prefer analytics.hiv_patient_dim_v1.given_name. Identifying information.

views.name: public.observation_flat
views.grain: Raw FHIR Observation, one row per observation x code coding x value coding. An observation repeats: never count rows here as results, and never aggregate val_quantity across unlike concepts. Prefer analytics.hiv_observation_fact_v1, which is one row per observation, pivots CIEL/SNOMED/WHO-ANC into their own columns, and excludes subject-less rows and impossible dates.

columns.description: FHIR Observation resource identifier. Repeats across codings.

columns.name: patient_id

columns.name: encounter_id
columns.description: Encounter the observation was recorded in; null when unlinked.

columns.name: status
columns.description: FHIR Observation.status, such as final or preliminary. Filter to final before reporting results.

columns.name: obs_date
columns.description: Effective date-time of the observation. This data contains impossible dates (as early as 1919, as late as 5025); the curated fact view restricts to 2020-01-01..2035-01-01, and a query over this table should do the same.

columns.name: val_string

columns.name: val_boolean
columns.description: Boolean result, for yes/no observations.

columns.name: val_datetime

columns.name: code_code
columns.description: Concept code within code_sys; read the pair together.

columns.description: Terminology system of the concept coding. The OpenMRS-native arm is an empty string or null, not a URL -- treat both the same when selecting native codes.

columns.name: code_display
columns.description: Human-readable concept name for the coding on this row; the reliable way to select a concept by name.

columns.name: value_code
columns.description: Coded answer, for observations whose value is itself a concept.

columns.name: value_sys
columns.description: Terminology system of the coded answer; same empty-string native arm as code_sys.

columns.name: value_display
columns.description: Human-readable coded answer for the row, such as an adherence category.
